label: heart-s2-c3

analysis.note: Ablations remove a child's readout from the logit (zero and mean ablation give the same AUC because readouts enter additively). Linear replacement = least-squares refit of the child's logit contribution on its own raw inputs. The nonlinear block adds +0.004 train AUC over the linear core, all of it from the non-anginal-pain thalach gate; a linear refit of all three readouts keeps it (0.938), so the hidden layer is close to linear on train.

resisted: Nothing resisted coverage. The ST-depression gate for patients without non-anginal pain is a near-null part (readout -0.018, SD 0.009 logit units; ablating it raises train AUC by 0.0001) and is annotated as such. Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: cp:2 +0.27 and fbs:1 -0.21 in the linear core, extra protection for non-anginal-pain patients with lower cholesterol, and the gate that slightly lowers risk with more ST depression.
tool_bugs: No v3 tool bugs met. compute_shap on all 242 train rows took about a minute; it gives the nine unconnected inputs mean |SHAP| about 0.001 (estimator noise, not an effect). The agent sandbox refused shell loops calling uv with variables, so tools were called through a small Python subprocess wrapper in scratch (same xn.py). Input fan-out splits (-6, -15, -18, -9) taken from the topology and detect_splits.
summary: Mostly logistic regression: 16 direct edges (logit SD 3.67; train AUC 0.934 alone) plus three additive ReLU gates (logit SD 0.42) to 0.938. All three gates are switched by non-anginal chest pain (cp:3), which has no direct edge: a protective gate ReLU(-0.35 + 1.08 cp:3 + 0.68 thalach) read out -0.51, open for 97% of non-anginal-pain patients, and a smaller low-cholesterol gate for the same patients (-0.24), plus a near-null oldpeak hinge for everyone else. Age is not used at all. Unlike the 10-seed heart-s2 record (key 9083, an age/heart-rate-reserve gate and oldpeak hinges), this genome's only nonlinear effect is a chest-pain-type-specific level and thalach/cholesterol slope.
